h: More Anchors — Reform, Finance and the Live Debates

items.d: **iGOT-Karmayogi** past 1 crore registered users and 3 crore course completions; **Karmayogi Prarambh** as the induction module and **Aarambh** as the common foundation course across services. The reform's real test is whether **FRAC-based role matching** changes posting decisions, not whether courses are completed.

DARPG's annual **Swachhata and pendency-disposal campaigns** have cleared crores of files, freed lakhs of square feet of office space and earned scrap revenue in the hundreds of crores — the rare administrative reform with a measurable, published output. Cite as evidence that **process cleaning is a governance intervention**, not housekeeping.

One portal for central and state clearances, replacing the applicant's task of discovering which of 30+ departments must approve what. The administrative principle: **the burden of coordination belongs to the state, not the citizen** — the same principle behind Sevottam and one-stop centres.

**Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023** removed imprisonment from **183 provisions across 42 central Acts**, converting them to monetary penalties; Jan Vishwas 2.0 continues. The PubAd point: **regulatory overreach is a governance failure**, and trust-based regulation shifts the state from suspicion to verification.

Adopted across central ministries, with the DARPG target of cutting the levels a file passes through to **four**. The classic critique it addresses is **Merton's ritualism** — the file as an end in itself; digitisation makes delay visible and therefore answerable.

CPGRAMS' **Independent Feedback Unit** calls citizens back after disposal, which converts closure statistics into satisfaction data. The principle: **an output measure that the implementing agency controls will be gamed; an outcome measure gathered independently will not.**

groups.g: Finance, accountability and the federal edge

items.d: Centrally sponsored scheme funds now flow through one nodal account per scheme per state with **just-in-time release** and mandatory PFMS tracking. Centre's case: float and diversion end. States' case: it converts a transfer into a **controlled disbursal** and starves them of working capital. This is the sharpest live fiscal-federalism dispute after cesses.

State borrowing routed through corporations and special purpose vehicles to stay outside the FRBM limit. The **16th Finance Commission** recommended discontinuing it and bringing all such borrowing on-budget — the accountability principle being that **a liability the legislature cannot see, it cannot control**.

NITI Aayog's index (2025) ranks states on **quality of expenditure, revenue mobilisation, fiscal prudence, debt index and debt sustainability** — competitive federalism applied to state finance. Useful whenever the question asks how the Centre influences states without legislating.

Three standing gaps: **PPP projects** sit awkwardly within audit jurisdiction; **the lag** between audit and PAC scrutiny blunts consequence; and **performance audit findings carry no enforcement**. Every CAG answer should name at least one, or it reads as a description rather than an assessment.

**PAC** looks backwards at money already spent, on the CAG's report, chaired by the Opposition by convention; the **Estimates Committee** looks forward at whether the estimate itself is economical, has no CAG support, and is Lok Sabha only. Confusing the two is a common and costly error.

Statutory under the **States Reorganisation Act, 1956**, chaired by the Union Home Minister — five councils plus the separate **North Eastern Council**. Their meetings have become more frequent and now carry inter-state issues (border disputes, river water, security) that the Inter-State Council rarely convenes for. Cite as evidence that **federal coordination has migrated to the statutory forum**.

The proposed 2022 amendment to **Rule 6 of the IAS (Cadre) Rules, 1954** would let the Centre call an officer on central deputation without the state's concurrence in specified circumstances. States read it as an attack on the federal bargain behind Article 312; the Centre reads it as a response to falling deputation numbers. Unresolved, and a ready 15-marker.

From 2025, an assured **50% of the last 12 months' average pay** for 25 years of service, with a minimum guarantee and inflation indexation — a partial return to defined benefit after the NPS shift of 2004. The PubAd angle: **pension design is a motivation instrument** (Herzberg's hygiene factor) and a fiscal liability at once.

The move from ACR to **PAR** brought disclosure and numerical grading, and 360-degree feedback for empanelment. The unfixed problem is **rating inflation** — when almost everyone is 'outstanding', the instrument stops discriminating and promotion reverts to seniority.

Women are roughly a third of recent IAS batches and a much smaller share of senior policy posts; in the police they are about **12%** against the 33% many states have declared. **Representative bureaucracy** theory (Kingsley, Krislov) is the frame: passive representation matters because it changes what the institution notices.

The **frontline** — patwari, ASHA, anganwadi worker, constable, panchayat secretary — carries most citizen contact with the least training and the widest discretion. Lipsky's **street-level bureaucracy** is the theory; the practical implication is that capacity building spent at the top has the smallest marginal return.
